title: Seven LMCs, one building: multilevel load management for 37 chargers
description: How an apartment complex in Pirita, Tallinn runs 37 VOOL chargers on six sub-boards, with a master LMC keeping the whole building within its 800 A limit.
markdown:
A small site has one distribution board and one limit to respect. A large apartment complex has several: a main board for the whole building and a sub-board for each stairwell, block or garage section. Every one of them has its own fuse, and charging has to respect all of them at once.

VOOL solves this with multilevel load management. A master LMC sits at the main board and an LMC sits on each sub-board. Here is how one building in Tallinn is set up.

## The site

An apartment complex in Pirita, Tallinn has 37 VOOL Chargers, each up to 22 kW, fed from six sub-boards. There are seven VOOL LMC Pro controllers: one on each sub-board and one master at the main board.

![One master LMC with an 800 A limit above six sub-boards with limits from 125 A to 315 A and 3 to 11 chargers each](/img/news/multilevel-en.webp)

| Level | Limit | Chargers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main board, master LMC | 800 A | all 37 |
| Sub-board 1 | 250 A | 11 |
| Sub-board 2 | 315 A | 6 |
| Sub-board 3 | 250 A | 6 |
| Sub-board 4 | 125 A | 6 |
| Sub-board 5 | 315 A | 5 |
| Sub-board 6 | 200 A | 3 |

## Why one level is not enough

The six sub-board limits add up to 1,455 A. The building as a whole is limited to 800 A.

So each sub-board could be safely inside its own limit while the building's main supply is overloaded. The reverse is also true: a single LMC at the main board would keep the building within 800 A, but it could not see that one 125 A sub-board with six chargers was about to trip.

## How the two levels work together

- **Each sub-board LMC** measures its own board and shares that board's free capacity between its chargers. Its limit is never exceeded, whatever the rest of the building is doing.
- **The master LMC** measures the building's main supply. When the whole building gets close to 800 A, it lowers what the sub-board LMCs may hand out.
- **Chargers follow the lowest limit above them.** A car gets full power when both its sub-board and the building have room.

Nobody sets this by hand day to day. The limits are configured once at commissioning and the controllers do the rest.

## The first year in numbers

- **37 chargers online**, the first since 21 October 2025
- **2,091 charging sessions**
- **21.7 MWh** charged
- **217 kWh** on the busiest day so far (9 May 2026)

## Adding chargers later

When another parking space needs a charger, it is added to its sub-board. The main board is not touched: the sub-board LMC shares its capacity with one more charger, and the master keeps looking after the total.
